page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-16-lssd is a general-purpose server instance configured with 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs built on the ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 architecture running at 3.0 GHz. The processor features 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 80 MB of shared L3 cache, backed by hardware-accelerated AES cryptography instructions. The system provides 64 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 CPU-to-memory allocation of 4 GB per vCPU, and integrates 1608 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage across 4 disks. No discrete GPU acceleration is included, and public IPv4 addresses require separate allocation.

Benchmark evaluations show competitive throughput across compute, data processing, and memory subsystems. The platform achieved top-quartile performance in Geekbench single-core (1961.0) and multi-core (17040.0) testing, alongside strong results in gzip compression (32.37 GB/sec) and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression (221.45 GB/sec). Memory subsystem efficiency is a notable strength, with PassMark memory scoring in the top decile at 3247.82 and large-block uncached memory read bandwidth measuring 314.24 GB/sec. Static web serving throughput reached 43.54 GB/sec, while PassMark database operations also performed in the upper quartile.

The 1:1 physical-to-virtual core mapping eliminates hyper-threading contention, delivering predictable execution for compute-bound tasks. Bundling high-capacity local NVMe storage with arm64 power efficiency yields strong IOPS and data density without requiring additional networked storage attachments. However, workloads requiring x86-specific instruction sets like AVX-512 or AMX will require software re-architecture or alternate x86 instance families.

This server profile suits I/O-intensive databases, transactional key-value stores, web serving clusters, intermediate caching tiers, continuous integration pipelines, and light machine learning inference tasks processing medium-sized language models.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-16-lssd is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by a 16-core ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 processor clocked at 3.0 GHz with dedicated core allocation. It features 64 GB of RAM, offering a balanced 4 GB per vCPU ratio, and includes 1608 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD storage across 4 drives. Benchmark profiles indicate strong execution capabilities, highlighted by top-quartile Geekbench scores, high memory bandwidth reaching 314.24 GB/sec on uncached reads, and top-decile PassMark memory results. The platform also demonstrates strong static web serving throughput at 43.54 GB/sec and fast database operational benchmarks. Without discrete GPU resources or x86 instruction compatibility, the instance provides predictable, cost-efficient processing capacity specifically adapted for database engines, cache nodes, microservice architectures, CI/CD runners, and high-throughput static web servers.
